findings.description: The bucket declares no server_side_encryption_configuration, so objects (including the vendor roster uploaded to it) are stored without a Terraform-enforced SSE policy. Unlike the audit_trail bucket, there is no KMS or AES256 default encryption rule.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket and no ACL is specified at all, leaving nothing in code to block public ACLs or public bucket policies from being applied later.
No bucket policy denies requests with aws:SecureTransport = false, so objects can be read and written over unencrypted HTTP.
Versioning is not enabled, so object overwrites and deletions are unrecoverable, removing a key defence against accidental or malicious destruction of stored data.
This bucket holds ledger/financial exports but declares no server_side_encryption_configuration, so data at rest is not protected by a Terraform-enforced encryption default.
The private ACL alone does not prevent a public bucket policy or future ACL change; no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource is defined for this bucket.
There is no bucket policy denying non-TLS requests, allowing financial export data to be transmitted over cleartext HTTP.
Versioning is not enabled on a bucket containing ledger exports, so deleted or overwritten records cannot be recovered and tampering leaves no prior-version trail.
Model artifacts are stored without any server_side_encryption_configuration block, so no default SSE (AES256 or KMS) is enforced for this bucket's objects.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is defined, so public ACLs or a public bucket policy could be applied to this bucket without any account-level guardrail in this configuration.
Operational runbooks frequently contain hostnames, procedures, and occasionally credentials, yet this bucket declares no server_side_encryption_configuration.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource protects this bucket from public ACLs or public bucket policies being applied.

The ACL is set to "lcatalogopts-delivery-write", which is not a valid S3 canned ACL (the intended value is log-delivery-write). The grant on the audit/log destination bucket is therefore malformed, which can break log delivery integrity or, if corrected carelessly, grant broader write access than intended.
The bucket that stores audit and access logs has no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, so nothing in code prevents public exposure of log data.

A vendor roster spreadsheet (likely containing supplier and contact PII) is uploaded with no server_side_encryption argument into reports_archive, a bucket that itself has no default encryption rule, so the object is stored unencrypted.
